items.title: Borno: Zulum resettles Mayanti residents, inaugurates 500 houses
items.summary: Borno Governor Babagana Zulum inaugurated 500 houses and 2,000 semi-permanent shelters for residents of Mayanti, a community displaced by Boko Haram insurgency, along with a primary and junior secondary school. The governor also led APC campaign activities in Bama and Konduga, urging residents to vote for President Tinubu in the 2027 elections.
items.why: Demonstrates post-insurgency reconstruction efforts and political mobilization ahead of 2027 general elections in a conflict-affected region.

items.title: Reps weigh bill on divorce over sex denial
items.summary: The House of Representatives is considering a bill to expand grounds for divorce under the Matrimonial Causes Act, including denial of conjugal rights for three months, threats of bodily harm, and emotional or psychological trauma. The bill was read for the first time on Tuesday.
items.why: Reflects legislative efforts to modernize family law and address spousal rights and protection in Nigeria.

items.title: NEMA recovers 24 bodies from Bayelsa boat mishap
items.summary: The National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) reported that 24 survivors were rescued from a boat mishap in Bayelsa State on November 20, 2026, with ongoing search and rescue operations for additional passengers. Governor Douye Diri visited the scene and commended emergency responders for their collaborative efforts.
items.why: Highlights a tragic maritime accident and the coordinated emergency response efforts in Nigeria's riverine communities.

items.title: CAF Unveils U-17 Women’s AFCON, Opens Bidding For 2028 Edition
items.summary: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) unveiled the inaugural Africa U-17 Women's Cup of Nations tournament scheduled for March-April 2028, with qualifying matches starting April 2027. CAF opened bidding for Member Associations interested in hosting the tournament.
items.why: Represents CAF's commitment to developing women's football and creating competitive pathways for young African female players.

items.title: NUPRC Opens 2026 Oil Licensing Round, Offers 40 Oil, Gas Blocks To Investors
items.summary: The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) opened its 2026 oil and gas licensing round, offering 40 blocks (17 onshore, 14 shallow water, 9 deep offshore) to prospective investors with registration closing January 15, 2027. The bidding portal went live on November 20, 2026.
items.why: Signals government efforts to attract foreign investment in the oil and gas sector and boost revenue generation.
